commits.message:
feat(email-parsing): wire the LLM extraction fallback for ambiguous emails

Deterministic email parsing (app/email_parsing/parsers.py) has always
been -- and stays -- 100% LLM-free. This adds the strictly separate,
later stage the original spec called for (section 7.5 step 7): when a
parsed job requirement or hotlist scores below 0.70 confidence (the
same cutoff those parsers already use for requires_review), one
confidence-gated LLM pass gets a chance to fill in what determinism
couldn't, before the record ever reaches a human reviewer or a
recruiter's claim email.

Zero new LLM integration work: reuses the existing audited, cost-
tracked, cache-eligible LiteLLM/Langfuse path (run_llm_fallback) and,
critically, two Langfuse prompts that already exist and are already
proven -- jf.jobs.jd.extract (the generic /understanding pipeline's own
job-description fallback) and jf.broadcast.hotlist.extract (the
Telegram broadcast channel's own hotlist fallback, whose confidence-
gating design this module's structure mirrors directly). No new prompts
to write or review.

Two different merge strategies, matching what "low confidence" actually
means for each document kind:
  - Job requirement: fills only fields the deterministic parser left
    empty. A field it already found is never overwritten -- the LLM is
    a gap-filler, not a second opinion. A field neither pass finds stays
    null, never guessed (spec 13.2 anti-hallucination guarantee).
  - Hotlist: a low-confidence table/block split usually means the
    record *boundaries* are wrong (wrong consultant count, fields
    attributed to the wrong person), not just a few gaps -- so a used
    LLM result replaces the whole record list rather than merging into
    it, same as the broadcast channel already does.

Field-level provenance (app/email_parsing/provenance.py) now tags
exactly which fields came from which pass: an LLM-filled job field gets
extraction_method=llm_fallback, value_kind=LLM_EXTRACTED, and extractor
set to the actual prompt id -- while every deterministic field on the
same record keeps its original deterministic/EXTRACTED tagging. A
record can legitimately mix both. A replaced hotlist record's fields
are all tagged llm_fallback, since the whole record came from that pass.

Verified: 8 new tests (app/email_parsing/llm_fallback.py's gating and
merge logic, and the provenance tagging split) with run_llm_fallback
mocked -- these check the logic in this module, not the real LiteLLM/
Langfuse call, which costs real money and belongs to that module's own
coverage. Full existing 8-script regression suite plus the retry/DLQ
suite re-run clean afterward, confirming zero regressions.
